subject: Post-call: API contracts, auth & routing decisions for Voltix integration
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Morales <sofia@voltix.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: API contracts, auth & routing decisions for Voltix integration

Sofia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick summary and the asks we discussed so we have a clear mutual action plan.

Recap (what we covered)
- Integration modes: Hosted Redwood API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput) or Private (VPC) for data residency. You indicated priority for low-latency hosted with a migration path to Dedicated later.
- Auth: Voltix prefers a short-lived credential model (mentioned OIDC client creds) and raised mTLS as a potential requirement for procurement.
- Routing & fallbacks: We sketched routing by region and latency tier with an automatic fallback to a smaller, cheaper model if capacity constrained.
- Structured output & tool calling: You want tool-calling for a payments microservice and a deterministic JSON schema for product metadata.
- Embeddings/reranker: Using embeddings for candidate retrieval + a lightweight reranker at inference time to boost accuracy was the chosen approach.
- Request/response questions: We flagged chat vs completions semantics, streaming behaviour (partial tokens vs event chunks), tokenization counts and max_tokens enforcement, and stop-sequence corner cases.

Action items / asks from Voltix
1) Confirm preferred auth: OIDC client-credentials or mTLS? Any internal PKI constraints we should know about?
2) Confirm whether streaming must deliver partial tokens or you prefer chunked events (we discussed both patterns).
3) Share your initial schema for tool-calling (payments order fields) — we attached a stub spec to get started.
4) Security questionnaire (you said procurement would send this) — we'll prioritize SOC-2 artefacts if needed.

Redwood immediate next steps
- Technical deep dive (solutions + infra) to finalize SDK setup and routing policy.
- Send a short integration spec and mutual action plan (attached).
- Provide guidance on chat vs completions tradeoffs & recommended default limits for your workload.

Attachments: voltix_integration_req.docx (integration stub), redwood_mutual_action_plan.xlsx
Related links: HubSpot deal BADGE: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4782

Proposed time for TD: Tue Jul 7th, 10:00am PT — would that work for you?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0178

From: Sofia Morales <sofia@voltix.ai>

Cc: integrations@voltix.ai
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: API contracts, auth & routing decisions for Voltix integration

Karthik — thanks for the succinct recap. A few clarifications from our side below.

Auth:
- Procurement will push for mTLS for vendor endpoints unless we can present a clear short-lived credential model and centralized auditing. Our security lead prefers OIDC client-credentials where we manage the client and Redwood rotates keys — acceptable if audit logs + certs are available.

Streaming:
- Latency is critical for our live search product. We prefer true streaming (partial token / token deltas) because our UX stitches the partial results into the UI as they arrive. If Redwood can expose partial tokens with deterministic end-of-stream events, that's preferred. If not, chunked events with a small max chunk latency (<=50ms) is acceptable.

Embeddings/reranker:
- Plan: nightly embedding index for candidates, then an online reranker using a 2-3 prompt fusion. We need to confirm per-request latency target for the reranker: <120ms P95.

Schema / Stop sequences:
- For tool-calling we need a strict JSON schema (no free-text) for the payments endpoint. If chat is used for higher-level orchestration, how do you recommend enforcing a stop sequence vs explicit response delimiter to avoid trailing commentary?

Attaching our security questionnaire "Voltix_Sec_Q.pdf" — procurement will fill it with follow-ups.

Yes to Tue Jul 7 10am PT for the technical deep-dive. Please include an agenda that covers: auth options + audit logs, streaming semantics (practical examples), embedding pipeline (indexing cadence + model choices), and schema enforcement for tool calls.

Thanks,
Sofia Morales
Head of Integrations | Voltix
sofia@voltix.ai

Subject: RE: Post-call: API contracts, auth & routing decisions for Voltix integration

Sofia — great questions. A few concrete answers and recommendations from the SE side.

1) Auth patterns (recommendation)
- Short term: OIDC client_credentials with rotating secrets + token introspection. This maps cleanly to our hosted flow and minimizes procurement friction.
- Enterprise/Final: mTLS is supported in Redwood Private / Dedicated. If Voltix requires mTLS for vendor endpoints we can design a dedicated ingress with mutual TLS termination and provide cert pinning docs.
- Audit logs: we'll provide request-level logs with request_id, model, route, and token usage (audit export for monthly ingestion).

2) Streaming semantics
- Redwood supports two streaming styles: token-stream (individual token deltas via SSE) and chunked events (application-level framing).
- For true partial-token streaming use the chat endpoint with streaming=true. It emits token-deltas as SSE events and includes an explicit [EOS] event at the end. Example SSE line: `event: token\ndata: {`
